To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
immunohistochemical analysis for α chains of collagen IV is useful to diagnose Alport's syndrome.
the heating conditions for the antigen retrieval of collagen type IV α chains were carefully determined using renal sections from AS and nonAS patients.
the optimal heating conditions for antigen retrieval varied among the basement membranes and were dependent on the type examined.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the immunohistochemical analysis in paraffin embedded renal sections of Alport's patients, using monoclonal antibodies to α chains of type IV collagen, and with the establishment of the antigen retrieval method by autoclave-heating.
the antigen retrieval of collagen type IV by autoclave treatment, which is useful for the immunohistochemical detection of α chains of collagen in the renal sections of AS.
the development of a new method for the diagnosis of AS using paraffin- embedded renal sections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the immunohistochemical method using the mAbs is applicable to the diagnosis of AS on paraffin sections, if the antigen retrieval method described here is used.
the antigen retrieval with autoclavable heating is a useful method to detect the epitopes for the mAbs generated by our laboratory.
the antigen retrieval method is very useful for the immunohistochemical detection of collagen type IV in paraffin sections, although it is not a panacea.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the antigen retrieval by autoclaving is a powerful tool in immunohistochemical studies, and that this method could be applied to the diagnosis of various diseases.

the antigen retrieval method using the autoclave heating could extend the possibility for the immunohistochemical analysis using paraffin- embedded sections, not only for the diagnosis of AS but also for other immunohistochemical analyses.
the mAbs generated by us are useful for the diagnosis not only in fresh-frozen but also in paraffin sections, when the antigen retrieval method is applied.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the antigen retrieval method using an autoclave heating is applicable to the immunohistochemical detection of collagen type IV chains in renal tissue sections.
the immunohistochemical method using mAbs is a powerful tool to detect the basement membrane abnormalities in AS patients.
antigen retrieval by autoclaving is a useful technique for the diagnosis of Alport syndrome.
